title: Flipping Alice's special bit preserves singleton mass
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, and let $\omega$ be a point of the hard sample space, i.e. a choice of special coordinate $T \in \{0,\dots,n-1\}$, bits $X_T, Y_T \in \{0,1\}$, and an assignment of one of the three disjointness states to each coordinate. Write $\omega'$ for the point obtained from $\omega$ by flipping only Alice's special-coordinate bit $X_T$, leaving $T$, $Y_T$, and all the other-coordinate data unchanged. Then the ambient volume measure assigns the singleton $\{\omega'\}$ the same real-valued mass as the singleton $\{\omega\}$.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
ω is a point of the hard sample space HardSample n
